answer: A bond of 56% of expected earnings must sit in a custody account that the identity cannot spend from, only forfeit. Deposits are visible in prism, and ember reconciles the forfeits at each close. Because the custody account is separate, anyone cannot recycle one pool of capital across 38 aliases, and each one needs its own funded ferrous account. The honest user pays this once; a farm pays it 41 times over for the same share of the pool. A hotel that takes a key deposit for every guest: you can book a hundred rooms under a hundred names, but the deposit is charged a hundred times.
